title: Ethical and social risks of harm from Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Literature review of bias in coreference resolution, generative story outputs, stereotype benchmarks (e.g., StereoSet, HONEST), and conversational agent personas.
Review of empirical studies on generative language models (e.g., GPT-3) mapping specific religious terms to negative or violent associations.
Review of benchmark evaluations (e.g., StereoSet) and studies on disparate toxicity classification rates for dialects like African American Vernacular English (AAVE).
Synthesis of literature measuring disparate model performance between high-resource languages (e.g., English, Mandarin) and other languages, dialects, or sociolects.
Conceptual analysis of exclusionary norms and review of literature on the disproportionate flagging/demotion of LGBT+ content by toxicity detection models.
Reviewing literature on disparate NLP model performance based on language variations tied to social class and educational backgrounds.
Review of benchmark tests (e.g., CrowS-Pairs) that measure the reproduction of cultural stereotypes via masked language model likelihood estimates.
